correctness.rationale: Every binary 2-binomial signature equals (one-count, weighted one-position sum); formula for 01 is weighted sum minus choose(one-count,2). The two paperfolding interleaving maps are derived from p_{2i}=p_i and the period-four odd positions and cover every start exactly. The explicit length-four base and simultaneous induction yield two disjoint parity-separated outer tiers of n signatures each and a central common arithmetic progression of k+1 signatures. Counts sum to 2n+k+1 for all k>=2. Standalone independent sliding-factor enumeration matches exact sets through n=512; recurrence checked through n=2048. Neither scan nor log is treated as proof of infinite completeness.

evidence: Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland prove general bounded binomial complexity under Parikh-collinear morphisms; the observed paperfolding complexity here grows linearly on dyadic lengths and is not an instance of that bounded conclusion.
Madill–Rampersad study level-one (abelian) paperfolding complexity, which is coarser and cannot imply the second-level number.
Lü–Chen–Wen–Wu study generalized Thue–Morse words and give an eventual-periodic law for that different automatic family.

value.rationale: Determines the first non-abelian binomial-complexity refinement for a canonical automatic sequence on infinitely many natural dyadic lengths, classifies all signatures by letter count and weighted one positions, and establishes a sharp half-of-ordinary-factor-complexity asymptotic along these lengths. The arithmetic split is not implied by earlier abelian recurrence or a finite census. Non-dyadic and higher-binomial cases remain open beyond this claim.
